title: There Is, There Are
overview: Say what there is in a kitchen: There is a fridge. There are two cups. Say an apple, but some rice. Say who has a thing: Ana's cup. It is mine. Point with this, that, these, those and the red one.
learningPath: Words: listen, look and say. 25 words.
Patterns: 5 cards. Read the one done for you.
Reading: read the 3 texts. Answer the questions.
Speaking: tap the mic. Say it. Listen.
Writing: write about a kitchen. A made-up one is OK.
Practice: write. Check with the answers.
lectureScript:
Hello! This is Unit 8.
In this unit, you talk about a kitchen.
You say what there is, and who has what.
It can be a kitchen you know, or a made-up one.
Listen.
There is a fridge in the kitchen.
There is a table.
There are two chairs.
There are four plates on the shelf.
One thing: there is.
Two or more: there are.
To ask, put is or are first.
Is there a fridge? Yes, there is.
Are there two cups? No, there aren't.
Not one? Say no.
There is no meat. There are no eggs.
Now food.
You can count apples. One apple, two apples.
You can count eggs and bananas.
An apple, an egg: say an.
You cannot count rice. You cannot count milk or water.
With rice, milk and water, say some.
There is some rice. There is some milk.
Is it in a cup, a glass or a bowl? Now you can count it.
A cup of tea. Two cups of tea.
Some words are new for two.
One child, two children.
One person, two people.
One knife, two knives.
Now, who has it?
Ana has a cup. It is Ana's cup.
Ivan has a key. It is Ivan's key.
The name comes first. The thing comes last.
Not: the cup of Ana. Say: Ana's cup.
In a kitchen at school or at work, write your name on your food.
Like this: Lena's milk.
Now this, that, these and those.
This cup is here, near me.
That cup is there, not near me.
These plates are here. Those plates are there.
One thing: this or that.
Two or more: these or those.
Say one, and you do not say the thing again.
Which cup? The red one.
This bowl is big. That one is small.
Last: mine, yours, his, hers, ours and theirs.
My cup. It is mine.
Your cup. It is yours.
Her cup. It is hers.
Is this bag yours? No, it is his.
Is this milk yours? No, it is Lena's. It is hers.
No thing comes next to mine.
Not: mine cup. Say: my cup, or it is mine.
Now go to Words. Goodbye!

outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can read a name on food: ANA'S MILK.

words.meaning: A white or brown food. People make it, cook it and eat it.
words.example: There is some bread on the table.
practice: The bread is on a plate.
Is there bread in the kitchen?
Dan eats bread in the morning.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to hide some bread in a made-up kitchen. Ask Is there bread on the table? Is there bread on the shelf? Go on until you find it.

words.meaning: A small white or brown food. You cook it in hot water.
words.example: There is some rice in the bowl.
practice: Is there rice in the box?
Priya cooks rice in the evening.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor two places for rice in a made-up kitchen. Check that you say There is some rice, not There are.

words.meaning: A white drink. A baby drinks it. It can go in tea.
words.example: There is some milk in the fridge.
practice: Is the milk in the fridge?
Yara drinks milk in the morning.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor: Is there milk in the fridge? Let it answer Yes, there is or No, there isn't. Then swap: it asks, and you answer.

words.meaning: It is wet. You drink it, and you wash with it.
words.example: A glass of water, please.
practice: There is some water in the bottle.
Wash the plates in hot water.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor for a glass of water, with please at the end. Then ask for milk and tea the same way.

words.meaning: A hot drink. It can be brown, green or red. You make it with hot water.
words.example: A cup of tea, please.
practice: Is there tea on the shelf?
There is some tea in the box.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to offer you three drinks, one at a time. Answer Yes, please or No, thanks. Then say the drink: a cup of tea, please.

words.meaning: A hot black or brown drink. You can drink it with milk.
words.example: There is some coffee in the cup.
practice: Ivan drinks coffee in the morning.
The coffee is next to the tea.
words.tutor: Coffee and cup start with the same sound. Say a cup of coffee to the tutor three times. Ask it if that first sound was clear.

words.meaning: It is white or brown. It goes in tea or coffee.
words.example: There is some sugar in the bowl.
practice: Is there sugar in the coffee?
The sugar is next to the salt.
words.starter: I have got some sugar and …
words.tutor: Sugar and salt are both white. Ask the tutor to name five foods and drinks. Say sugar or salt for each one, like tea: sugar.

words.meaning: It is white, like sugar. It goes on meat, fish and eggs, not in tea.
words.example: There is some salt on the table.
practice: Is there salt in the kitchen?
The salt is in a small box.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor where the salt is in a made-up kitchen. Use on, in or next to. Then ask it: Where is the salt?

words.meaning: A small white or brown food. Open it: it is yellow and white.
words.example: There are six eggs in the fridge.
practice: Is there an egg in the bowl?
Ivan cooks two eggs in the morning.
words.tutor: Say an egg, not a egg. Ask the tutor for five more words that take an. Say each one with an.

words.meaning: A small red, green or yellow fruit. You eat it.
words.example: There is an apple on the table.
practice: There are three apples in the bowl.
words.tutor: Say to the tutor: an apple, a red apple, a green apple. Ask it why an changes to a before red.

words.meaning: A long yellow fruit. You open it and eat it.
words.example: There are two bananas in the bowl.
practice: Is there a banana on the table?
words.tutor: Say banana with the tutor in three parts: ba-NA-na. Then take turns to count: one banana, two bananas, up to ten.

words.meaning: Food from an animal, not a fish. You cook it.
words.example: There is some meat in the fridge.
practice: The meat is on a plate.
Is there meat in this food?
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to make up a plate of food. Ask it Is there meat in it? and Is there fish in it? Listen for Yes, there is or No, there isn't.

words.meaning: It lives in water. People cook it and eat it.
words.example: There is some fish on the plate.
practice: Is there fish in the fridge?
Hana cooks fish in the evening.
words.tutor: Fish as food takes some. Tell the tutor three foods on a made-up plate. Say some fish, some rice or an egg.

words.meaning: Food from a garden or from a farmer. It can be green, red, orange or white.
words.example: There is a green vegetable on the plate.
practice: The vegetables are in the fridge.
words.tutor: Say vegetable to the tutor. You say it in three parts, VEJ-ta-bul, not four. Ask the tutor if you said three.

words.meaning: Food like an apple or a banana.
words.example: There is some fruit in the bowl.
practice: Is there fruit in the fridge?
The fruit is on the table.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to name ten foods. For each one, say fruit, vegetable or meat. Ask it to check your answers.

words.meaning: A room. People cook food in it.
words.example: There is a fridge in the kitchen.
practice: Is there a table in the kitchen?
Wash your cup in the kitchen.
Where is the kitchen? It is next to the office.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a kitchen you know or a made-up one. Use four lines with There is or There are. Ask it to find any line with is for two things.

words.meaning: A big white box in a kitchen. Milk and meat go in it.
words.example: The milk is in the fridge.
practice: Is there a fridge in the kitchen?
Open the fridge. There is some fish.
The fridge is next to the door.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor what is in a made-up fridge. Say two lines with There is some and two with There are. Then ask it about its own made-up fridge.

words.meaning: Food goes on it. You eat from it.
words.example: There are four plates on the shelf.
practice: The bread is on a plate.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to hide a made-up plate in a kitchen. Ask Is the plate on the table? Go on until you find it.

words.meaning: You drink water or milk from it, not hot tea.
words.example: There are two glasses on the table.
words.tutor: Say glass and glasses to the tutor. Glasses has one more part at the end: glass-es. Ask it to check you said that part.

words.meaning: You eat rice or eggs with it.
words.example: There is a spoon in the bowl.
practice: Is there a spoon for the sugar?
The spoons are on the table.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor what you eat with a spoon. Then ask what you eat with a fork. Say each answer back as a whole line.

words.meaning: You cut bread or meat with it.
words.example: The knife is on the plate.
practice: The knives are in the box.
A knife and a fork, please.
words.tutor: You do not say the k in knife: it sounds like nife. Say knife and knives to the tutor and ask if the start was right.

words.meaning: You eat meat or fish with it. It goes next to the knife.
words.example: There is a fork next to the plate.
practice: The forks are in the box.
The fork is on the table.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to lay a made-up table in words. Then say where the fork, the knife and the spoon go. Like this: The fork is next to the plate.

words.meaning: It is like a big cup. Rice or fruit goes in it.
words.example: The bowl is full of fruit.
practice: The bowl is on the shelf.
words.tutor: Bowl has the sound in no, not the sound in how. Say a bowl of rice three times. Ask the tutor if that sound was right.

words.meaning: A boy or a girl.
words.example: There is one child in the kitchen.
practice: The children are in the park.
There are three children at the table.
words.tutor: Say child and children to the tutor. Child has the sound in five. Children has the sound in six. Ask it to check both.

words.meaning: A man, a woman or a child.
words.example: There is one person at the desk.
practice: There are four people in the kitchen.
Is there a person at the door?
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to make up three rooms with people in them. For each room, say There is one person or There are … people.

grammar.title: There is one, there are two
grammar.explanation:
Say what is in a place.
One thing: there is.
Two or more: there are.
To ask, put is or are first: Is there…? Are there…?
grammar.rule:
One thing: there is
There is a fridge in the kitchen.
There is an apple on the table.

Two or more: there are
There are two plates on the shelf.
There are four chairs in the kitchen.

Not one: there is no, there are no
There is no fridge.
There are no eggs.

Ask
Is there a spoon? Yes, there is. No, there isn't.
Are there two cups? Yes, there are. No, there aren't.
(aren't: are not)
grammar.workedExample:
___ two glasses on the table.
1. Look: two glasses.
2. Two is more than one.
3. Two or more: there are.
4. Write: There are two glasses on the table.
5. Check: are and two. Yes.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to say is for two things.
No: There is two plates.
Yes: There are two plates.
It is easy to leave out there.
No: Is a fridge in the kitchen.
Yes: There is a fridge in the kitchen.
grammar.tip: One: there is. Two or more: there are.
grammar.practice:
Write is or are.
1. There ___ a fridge in the kitchen.
2. There ___ three cups on the shelf.
3. There ___ an egg in the bowl.
4. There ___ two bananas on the table.
5. ___ there a spoon? Yes, there is.
6. ___ there four chairs? No, there aren't.
7. There ___ ten plates in the box.
grammar.answers:
1. is  2. are  3. is  4. are  5. Is  6. Are  7. are
Wrong on 5 or 6? In a question, is or are comes first: Is there…? Are there…?
Wrong on 3? An egg is one thing: there is.

grammar.title: An apple, but rice; a child, two children
grammar.explanation:
You can count apples: one apple, two apples.
You cannot count rice, milk or water.
With those, say some, and there is: There is some rice.
Some words are new for two: one child, two children.
grammar.rule:
You can count it: a, an, two
a banana — three bananas
an apple — two apples
an egg — six eggs
a glass — two glasses

You cannot count it: some
some rice
some milk
some bread
some water
There is some rice. (is, not are)

New words for two or more
a child — two children
a person — two people
a knife — two knives
grammar.workedExample:
Write a rice or some rice?
1. Can you count rice? One rice, two rices? No.
2. You cannot count it.
3. So say some: some rice.
4. Some rice takes is.
5. Write: There is some rice in the bowl.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to count rice or bread.
No: a rice, two breads.
Yes: some rice, some bread.
It is easy to say childs or persons.
No: two childs, two persons.
Yes: two children, two people.
grammar.tip: Can you count it? a, an. No? some.
grammar.practice:
Write a, an or some.
1. ___ apple
2. ___ milk
3. ___ banana
4. ___ rice
5. ___ egg
6. ___ water
Write the word for two or more.
7. one child, two ___
8. one person, three ___
9. one knife, four ___
grammar.answers:
1. an  2. some  3. a  4. some  5. an  6. some  7. children  8. people  9. knives
Wrong on 1 or 5? Apple and egg: say an.
Wrong on 2, 4 or 6? You cannot count milk, rice or water: some.
Number 9: knife, knives. The f changes to v.

grammar.title: Ana's cup, Ivan's key
grammar.explanation:
Say who has a thing.
Ana has a cup. It is Ana's cup.
The children have plates. They are the children's plates.
The name comes first. The thing comes last.
grammar.rule:
the name, 's, the thing
Ana's cup
Ivan's key
my sister's phone
the man's bag
the children's plates

The thing can go:
Is it Ana's cup? Yes, it is Ana's.

On food in a fridge:
LENA'S MILK
DAN'S EGGS
grammar.workedExample:
Lena has a bag. Write it with 's.
1. Who has it? Lena.
2. What is it? A bag.
3. Name first: Lena.
4. Add 's: Lena's.
5. The thing last: Lena's bag.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to leave out 's.
No: This is Ivan phone.
Yes: This is Ivan's phone.
It is easy to put the thing first.
No: the phone of Ivan.
Yes: Ivan's phone.
grammar.practice:
Write two words with 's.
1. Zoe has a key: ___ ___
2. Priya has a bag: ___ ___
3. Dan has a cup: ___ ___
4. My brother has a bike: my ___ ___
5. The woman has a phone: the ___ ___
6. The children have bowls: the ___ ___
grammar.answers:
1. Zoe's key  2. Priya's bag  3. Dan's cup  4. brother's bike  5. woman's phone  6. children's bowls
Wrong on 6? Children is for two or more, and you add 's: children's.
Check each one: is the ' there, before the s?

grammar.title: That and those; the red one
grammar.explanation:
This and these: here, near you.
That and those: there, not near you.
One thing: this or that. Two or more: these or those.
Say one, and you do not say the thing again: the red one.
grammar.rule:
here — there
this cup — that cup
these cups — those cups

This is my plate. That is your plate.
These are my spoons. Those are your spoons.

one: the thing again
Which cup? The red one.
This bowl is big. That one is small.
Which apples? The green ones.
That one, please.
grammar.workedExample:
Two cups are on a shelf, not near you. Say they are clean.
1. Near you? No: that or those.
2. One or two? Two.
3. Two, not near: those.
4. Say: Those cups are clean.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to say this or that for two things.
No: this cups, that plates.
Yes: these cups, those plates.
It is easy to leave out one.
No: Which bowl? The big.
Yes: Which bowl? The big one.
grammar.tip: Here: this, these. There: that, those.
grammar.practice:
Write this, that, these or those.
1. (here, one) ___ spoon is clean.
2. (there, two) ___ glasses are on the shelf.
3. (here, two) ___ apples are for you.
4. (there, one) ___ fridge is big.
Write one or ones.
5. Which cup? The blue ___.
6. I have got a big plate and a small ___.
7. Which bananas? The yellow ___.
grammar.answers:
1. This  2. Those  3. These  4. That  5. one  6. one  7. ones
Wrong on 2? Two things and not near: those.
Wrong on 7? Two or more bananas, so ones.

grammar.title: Mine, yours, hers, ours, theirs
grammar.explanation:
My cup: it is mine.
Your cup: it is yours.
Mine, yours, hers, ours and theirs go at the end. No thing comes next.
His does not change: his cup, it is his.
grammar.rule:
my — mine
your — yours
his — his
her — hers
our — ours
their — theirs

This is my cup. It is mine.
That is her plate. It is hers.
Is this bag yours? No, it is his.
These bowls are ours. Those are theirs.

With a name: It is Ana's.
grammar.workedExample:
Is this Ivan's phone? Answer with one word for Ivan's.
1. Ivan is a man: he.
2. He: his.
3. Say: Yes, it is his.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to put a thing after mine.
No: It is mine cup.
Yes: It is my cup. It is mine.
It is easy to add ' to yours or hers.
No: your's, her's.
Yes: yours, hers.
grammar.tip: My cup. The cup is mine.
grammar.practice:
Write mine, yours, his, hers, ours or theirs.
1. It is my bag. It is ___.
2. Is this your key? Is it ___?
3. That is Zoe's cup. It is ___.
4. This is Dan's plate. It is ___.
5. These are our bowls. They are ___.
6. Those are their glasses. They are ___.
grammar.answers:
1. mine  2. yours  3. hers  4. his  5. ours  6. theirs
Wrong on 3? Zoe is a woman: her cup, so hers.
No ' in any of them: yours, hers, ours, theirs.

readings.title: Lena's Kitchen
readings.setting: A small kitchen. Lena talks about it.
readings.passage:
This is my kitchen. It is small and clean.
There is a fridge next to the door.
There is a table, and there are two chairs.
In the fridge, there is some milk and some fish.
There are six eggs. There is no meat.
On the shelf, there are four plates and four bowls.
There are two cups. The blue one is mine.
The red one is my sister's.
On the table, there is a bowl of fruit.
There are three bananas and an apple in it.

readings.title: A Cup of Tea, a Bowl of Rice
readings.setting: Food words for a shop or a kitchen.
readings.passage:
You can count apples and eggs.
One apple, two apples. One egg, six eggs.
You cannot count rice or milk.
You do not say two rices. You do not say a milk.
Say some: some rice, some milk.
Is it in a cup, a glass, a bowl or a bottle?
Now you can count it.
A cup of tea. Two cups of tea.
A glass of water. Three glasses of water.
A bowl of rice. A bottle of milk.
At a shop, say: Two bottles of milk, please.

readings.title: A Kitchen Notice
readings.setting: A kitchen at school or at work.
readings.passage:
OUR KITCHEN — PLEASE READ

1. Your food: write your name on it. Like this: DAN'S MILK.
2. Is it not yours? Do not eat it or drink it.
3. The tea, coffee and sugar on the shelf are for you.
4. Wash your cup, your plate and your spoon. They go on the shelf.
5. The white cups are for the kitchen. Please do not put them on your desk.
6. On Friday, we clean the fridge. Food in the fridge on Friday goes in the bin.

Thanks!

comprehension.q: What is next to the door?
comprehension.why: Line 2: There is a fridge next to the door.

comprehension.q: Is there meat in the fridge?

comprehension.why: Lines 7 and 8: The blue one is mine. The red one is my sister's. Lena says mine, so the blue cup is hers.

comprehension.q: The blue one is mine. What is one here?
comprehension.why: Line 7: There are two cups. The blue one is the blue cup.
Line 4: You do not say two rices. Line 5: Say some.

comprehension.q: You ask for water in a glass. What do you say?
comprehension.why: Line 9: A glass of water. Add please when you ask.

comprehension.q: The rice is in two bowls. Can you count it now?
comprehension.why: Lines 6 and 7: Is it in a bowl? Now you can count it.

comprehension.q: Your milk goes in this fridge. What do you do first?
comprehension.a: Write your name on it, like DAN'S MILK.
comprehension.why: Point 1: Your food: write your name on it.

comprehension.q: It is Friday. Your eggs are in the fridge. Where do they go?
comprehension.why: Point 6: Food in the fridge on Friday goes in the bin.

comprehension.q: The milk in the fridge says ZOE'S MILK. Can you drink it?
comprehension.a: No. It is Zoe's, not yours.
comprehension.why: Point 2: Is it not yours? Do not eat it or drink it.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — There is, there are
speaking.instructions:
Listen. Say each line.
There is a fridge in the kitchen.
There is a table.
There are two chairs.
There are four plates on the shelf.
There is some milk in the fridge.
Is there a spoon? Yes, there is.
Tap the mic. Say the 6 lines.
Tap the mic again. Listen.
Check: is with one thing, and with milk?
Are with two or more?
speaking.tutor: Say the six lines to the tutor. Ask it to find any line with is for two things. Ask it to find any line with are for one.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — A kitchen you know
speaking.instructions:
Talk about a kitchen.
It can be a kitchen you know, or a made-up one.
Say 5 lines.
There is a ___ in the kitchen.
There are ___ in the kitchen.
In the fridge, there is some ___.
On the shelf, there are ___.
There is no ___.
Tap the mic. Say it. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 5 lines?
There is or there are in each line?
Is for one, are for two or more?
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
Talk about a kitchen.
It can be a kitchen you know, or a made-up one.
Say 5 lines.
There is a … in the kitchen.
There are … in the kitchen.
In the fridge, there is some …
On the shelf, there are …
There is no …
Tap the mic. Say it. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 5 lines?
There is or there are in each line?
Is for one, are for two or more?
speaking.tutor: Give the tutor your five lines about a made-up kitchen. Then ask it three questions about its kitchen: Is there a fridge? Are there chairs? Is there milk?

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — This, that, these, those
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat.
this, these
that, those
there
Listen to the first sound: the, this, that, these, those, there.
Say this short. Say these long.
Now say these 4 lines.
This cup is mine.
These cups are mine.
That bowl is yours.
Those bowls are yours.
Tap the mic. Say the 4 lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: is these long, and this short?
Does those have the sound in no?
speaking.tutor: Write this or these ten times, in any order. Say your list to the tutor. Ask it to write what it heard. Check it against your list.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Is it yours?
speaking.instructions:
Read A. Say B.
1. A: Is this cup yours? B: Yes, it is mine.
2. A: Is this bag Ivan's? B: Yes, it is his.
3. A: Is this phone Zoe's? B: No, it isn't hers.
4. A: Are these keys ours? B: Yes, they are ours.
5. A: Are those plates the children's? B: Yes, they are theirs.
Tap the mic. Say the 5 B lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: mine, his, hers, ours or theirs in each line?
A friend can say A. No one with you? Say A and B.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to name made-up things and ask Is this yours? or Is this hers? Answer each one with a whole line: Yes, it is mine. No, it is his.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — At a shop
speaking.instructions:
You are at a shop. You ask for fruit.
Listen. Say your lines.
Shop: Hello! Apples?
You: Yes, please. Two apples.
Shop: These red ones, or those green ones?
You: The green ones, please.
Shop: And a bag?
You: Yes, please. That one, the big one.
Shop: Here. Thanks!
You: Thanks. Goodbye!
Tap the mic. Say your lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 4 lines? Ones for the apples? One for the bag?
A friend can read the shop lines. No one with you? Read them and answer.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to be a shop assistant. It has cups, bags and apples in two colours. Choose each time: this one, that one, or the red ones.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — Lena's milk, Ivan's eggs
speaking.instructions:
Read the names on the food in a fridge.
LENA'S MILK
IVAN'S EGGS
ZOE'S BREAD
THE CHILDREN'S FRUIT
Listen to each question. Say your answer.
Is the milk Lena's?
Are the eggs Zoe's?
Is the bread Ivan's?
Is the fruit Lena's?
Tap the mic. Say the 4 answers. Tap again. Listen.
Check with these:
Yes, it is Lena's.
No, they are Ivan's.
No, it is Zoe's.
No, it is the children's.
Did you say Lena's, not Lena?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to make up four names on food, like PRIYA'S RICE. Then it asks: Is the rice Priya's? You answer with the name.

writing.title: Writing 1 — What is in the kitchen
writing.prompt:
Write about a kitchen.
It can be a kitchen you know, or a made-up one.
Write 5 sentences with there is or there are.
writing.model:
There is a fridge in the kitchen.
There is a table next to the window.
There are three chairs.
There are six glasses on the shelf.
There is some bread on the table.
writing.criteria:
5 sentences.
At least 2 with there is and 2 with there are.
There is for one thing, or for bread, rice or milk.
There are for two or more.
Each one starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop (.).
writing.support:
Copy the model.
Change one word in each line: fridge, table, chairs, glasses, bread.
Count first. One: is. Two or more: are.
writing.extension: Add 2 questions and answers: Is there a fridge? Yes, there is. Are there cups? No, there aren't.

writing.title: Writing 2 — A list for the shop
writing.prompt:
Write a list for a shop. Write 8 things.
4 things you can count: write a number, a or an.
4 things you cannot count: write some, or a bottle of.
writing.model:
SHOP LIST
six eggs
three bananas
an apple
two glasses
some rice
some bread
a bottle of milk
some tea
writing.criteria:
8 things.
4 with a number, a or an.
4 with some or a bottle of.
No rices, breads, milks or teas.
Children, people or knives, if you write them: no s at the end.
writing.support:
Draw two boxes on paper.
Box 1: I can count it. Box 2: I cannot count it.
Write 4 food words in each box.
Then add a number or some.
writing.extension: Write 2 sentences about your list: There are six eggs on my list. There is some rice on my list.

writing.title: Writing 3 — Names on the food
writing.prompt:
Four people have food in one fridge.
Write 4 names on food, with 's.
Then write a line for each: his, hers, ours or theirs.
Use made-up names.
writing.model:
YARA'S RICE: It is Yara's. It is hers.
DAN'S EGGS: They are Dan's. They are his.
THE CHILDREN'S MILK: It is the children's. It is theirs.
HANA'S BREAD: It is Hana's. It is hers.
writing.length: Four names on food, and a line for each
writing.criteria:
4 names on food, in capital letters.
An ' before the s in each name.
His, hers, ours or theirs in each line.
No ' in hers, ours or theirs.
writing.support:
Start with the model.
Change only the names and the food.
A man: his. A woman: hers. Two or more people: theirs.
writing.extension: Add one for you, with a made-up name, and write: It is mine.

writing.title: Writing 4 — A kitchen note
writing.prompt:
Write a note for a kitchen at school or at work, like Reading 3.
Write 4 lines.
Use there is or there are, and one name with 's.
writing.model:
KITCHEN NOTE
There is some milk in the fridge. It is for you.
The bread on the table is Priya's. Please do not eat it.
There are clean glasses on the shelf.
Wash your plate and your spoon. Thanks!
writing.criteria:
A title and 4 lines.
There is or there are in 2 lines.
One name with 's.
Each line starts with a capital letter. It ends with . or !
writing.support:
Copy points 1 and 4 of Reading 3.
Change the food and the name.
Then write 2 lines with there is and there are.
writing.extension: Add a line with that, these or those: Those cups are for you.

activities.title: Practice 1 — There is or there are
activities.instructions:
Write is or are.
1. There ___ a fridge in the kitchen.
2. There ___ six eggs in the bowl.
3. There ___ some milk in the glass.
4. There ___ two knives on the table.
5. ___ there a spoon in the box?
6. ___ there four chairs?
7. There ___ some bread on the plate.
8. There ___ three children in the park.
activities.answers:
1. is  2. are  3. is  4. are  5. Is  6. Are  7. is  8. are
Check 3 and 7: you cannot count milk or bread, so is.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 1 and do it again.
activities.solo: Write your answers on paper. Check with the key. Count the right ones.

activities.title: Practice 2 — Count it or not
activities.instructions:
Write each word in box A or box B.
A: I can count it. (an apple, two apples)
B: I cannot count it. (some rice)
1. egg
2. milk
3. banana
4. sugar
5. plate
6. water
7. spoon
8. bread
9. apple
10. salt
activities.answers:
A: egg, banana, plate, spoon, apple (1, 3, 5, 7, 9)
B: milk, sugar, water, bread, salt (2, 4, 6, 8, 10)
The test: can you say two? Two eggs: yes. Two milks: no.
9 or 10 right: good.
8 or less: read Pattern 2 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each word with a, an or some before you write it. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 3 — Who has it?
activities.instructions:
Write the name with 's.
1. Ana has a cup. It is ___ cup.
2. Priya has a phone. It is ___ phone.
3. My sister has a bag. It is my ___ bag.
4. The man has a key. It is the ___ key.
5. The children have plates. They are the ___ plates.
6. Ivan has some bread. It is ___ bread.
7. The woman has a bike. It is the ___ bike.
8. Lena has two bowls. They are ___ bowls.
activities.answers:
1. Ana's  2. Priya's  3. sister's  4. man's  5. children's  6. Ivan's  7. woman's  8. Lena's
Number 5: children is for two or more, and you add 's: children's.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 3 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each line out loud. Write the name with 's. Check the ' in each answer with the key.

activities.title: Practice 4 — This, that, these or those
activities.instructions:
Look at the words in ( ). Write this, that, these or those.
1. (here, one) ___ cup is mine.
2. (there, two) ___ plates are dirty.
3. (here, two) ___ bananas are green.
4. (there, one) ___ fridge is big.
5. (here, one) ___ knife is clean.
6. (there, two) ___ glasses are yours.
Write one or ones.
7. Which bowl? The white ___.
8. Which apples? The red ___.
activities.answers:
1. This  2. Those  3. These  4. That  5. This  6. Those  7. one  8. ones
Wrong on 2 or 6? Two things, not here: those.
Number 8: two or more apples, so ones.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 4 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each answer out loud. Point near you for this and these. Point away for that and those. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 5 — My or mine?
activities.instructions:
Choose the right word.
1. This is (my / mine) cup.
2. The cup is (my / mine).
3. Is this (your / yours) plate?
4. Is this plate (your / yours)?
5. That is Zoe's bag. It is (her / hers).
6. It is (her / hers) bag.
7. These are (our / ours) chairs.
8. The chairs are (our / ours).
activities.answers:
1. my  2. mine  3. your  4. yours  5. hers  6. her  7. our  8. ours
The test: does a thing come next? Yes: my, your, her, our. No: mine, yours, hers, ours.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 5 and do it again.
activities.solo: Look at the word next to the gap. Is it a thing? Write your answer. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Make the sentence
activities.instructions:
Make a sentence.
Start with a capital letter.
End with a full stop or ?
1. a fridge / there / is / in the kitchen
2. are / on the shelf / there / two bowls
3. there / a spoon / is / ?
4. some / there / rice / is / in the bowl
5. is / Lena's / this / cup
6. mine / is / the red one
7. those / yours / are / glasses
activities.answers:
1. There is a fridge in the kitchen.
2. There are two bowls on the shelf.
3. Is there a spoon?
4. There is some rice in the bowl.
5. This is Lena's cup.
6. The red one is mine.
7. Those glasses are yours.
Number 3: in a question, is comes first: Is there…?
Also right: 5. Is this Lena's cup? 7. Are those glasses yours?
6 or 7 right: good.
5 or less: read Patterns 1, 3 and 5 and do it again.
activities.solo: Write each sentence. Read it out loud. Check with the key.

quizzes.q: There ___ two glasses on the table.
quizzes.why: Two glasses is more than one: there are. Is is for one thing. It is and has do not go after there.

quizzes.q: ___ there a fridge in the kitchen? Yes, there is.
quizzes.why: One fridge: is. In a question, is comes first: Is there…? Are is for two or more. It and has do not ask this question.
You cannot count rice, so say some rice. A rice and two rices count it. Some comes before rice, not after it.
Child has a new word for two or more: children. Childs and childrens are not words. Child is for one.
You can count eggs: an egg, two eggs. You cannot count water, so not a water. One egg takes an, not some. Sugar takes some, not an.

quizzes.q: Lena has a phone. It is ___ phone.
quizzes.why: Name, then 's, then the thing: Lena's phone. Lena alone does not say she has it. Lenas has no '. Her's is not a word: say her phone.
Name first, then 's, then the thing: Ivan's bag. The bag of Ivan is not the English way. Ivan bag has no 's. Bag Ivan's puts the thing first.

quizzes.q: The cups are on a shelf, not near you. ___ cups are clean.
quizzes.why: Two or more, and not near you: those. This and these are for things near you. That is for one thing.

quizzes.q: A: Which plate? B: The big ___.
quizzes.why: One plate, so one: the big one. Ones is for two or more. The big it and the big this are not English.

quizzes.q: This is my cup. It is ___.
quizzes.why: No thing comes next, so mine. My needs a thing next to it: my cup. Me and I do not say who has it.

quizzes.q: Is this Zoe's bag? Yes, it is ___.
quizzes.why: Zoe is a woman: her bag, so it is hers. His is for a man. She does not say who has it. Her's is not a word: hers has no '.

quizzes.q: The name on the food in a fridge says YARA'S EGGS. What does it tell you?
quizzes.why: Yara's eggs: Yara has them. They are hers, not yours, so do not eat them. The name does not ask for eggs. It does not say there are no eggs.

teacherNotes.note: Every card has a worked example before its practice, every exercise has a key with a score line, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back and a checklist the learner can see. If you are helping, listen to a recording together and let the learner find the slip against the checklist before you point it out.

Nothing here assumes what a learner eats or what their home has. Every task offers a kitchen the learner knows or a made-up one, and the kitchen notice is set at school or at work. Do not ask what is in the learner's own kitchen or fridge, and accept a made-up kitchen without comment.

Three, all common whatever the first language: counting what English does not count (a rice, breads, informations later on); the possessive in the wrong order (the cup of Ana for Ana's cup); and a noun after mine or yours (mine cup). The quick test for the last one is to ask whether a thing comes next: if yes, my; if no, mine.

Some appears only with things that cannot be counted; some and any with other nouns, and many and much, are Unit 17, so How many? is deliberately absent. A cup of, a glass of and a bottle of are shown in Reading 2 as a way to count, not as a separate pattern. Aren't is shown beside isn't from Unit 7. Ones is taught as the plural of one on the demonstratives card. Cut in the meaning of knife and animal in the meaning of meat are carried by the picture.

The AI tutor is a rehearsal partner, not a marking service, and no task is scored by it alone. Tutor prompts use made-up kitchens, fridges and names throughout; keep that, and never ask the learner to give the tutor real details about their home or family.

selfAssessment.statement: I can say what there is in a kitchen.
I can write an apple, but some rice.
I can read a name on food: ANA'S MILK.
I can ask for that one or the red one.
I can answer: Is this yours? Yes, it is mine.
I can read a kitchen notice and answer questions.
I can write a list and a note about a kitchen.

assignment.title: A kitchen, and whose things are whose
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Tap the mic. Say 5 lines about a kitchen with there is, there are and some. Then say who has one thing: This cup is Ana's. It is hers.
2. Write 4 names on food for a fridge, like Writing 3, and a line for each.
It can be a kitchen you know, or a made-up one. Use made-up names.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and written names on food
